I estimated these from general knowledge of how MLPs behave under these settings. I did not run or look up the benchmark data, so treat every number as a prior-based guess.

The main reasoning behind the non-default calls:
- **Learning rate and depth (1, 6, 11):** deeper nets are less stable at high learning rates, so a higher rate or extra depth hurts more there.
- **Regularization (13, 27):** a very large alpha causes underfitting, so raising it from the high band hurts, and hurts small widths more.
- **Width (3, 4, 14, 21, 29):** extra width helps most when capacity or training speed is the bottleneck, and little once the network is already wide.
- **Batch size and learning rate (5, 22):** large batches mean fewer updates, so a higher learning rate helps more there.
- **Everything else:** I expect no interaction consistent across all three datasets.
